title: Assert and static_assert
recap: assert checks a runtime invariant in assertion-enabled builds and aborts on violation. It can disappear when NDEBUG is defined, so do not hide necessary assignments or input validation inside its argument.
static_assert checks a constant expression during compilation. It does not run later, and it can reject a broken compile-time assumption before an executable exists.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement constexpr validPercent(percent), true exactly for [0,100], and checkedPercent(percent), which asserts that precondition then returns the input. validPercent must work in constant expressions. checkedPercent must abort on invalid values in a debug build, not return a sentinel. The provided tests isolate invalid calls in child processes so Alt+R still reports results. Run these tests with assertions enabled (no NDEBUG, and a Debug CMake build). Assertions document programmer mistakes; they are not user-input validation.
hints: Make validPercent a constexpr range predicate.
Use assert(validPercent(percent)) before returning the value.
Assertions are intentionally tested in subprocesses; do not replace them with an ordinary return.
